p: we beseech you: The second part of the epistle, containing an excellent prophecy of the state of the Church, which will be from the apostles time to the latter day of judgment.

gathering together unto him: If we think earnestly upon that unmeasurable glory which we will be partakers of with Christ, it will be an excellent remedy for us against wavering and impatience, so that neither the glistening of the world will allure us, nor the dreadful sight of the cross dismay us.

That ye be not soon shaken: We must take heed of false prophets, especially in this matter, who go about to deceive, and that for the most part, after three sorts: for either they brag of fake prophetical revelations, or they bring conjectures and reasons of their own, or use counterfeit writings.
spirit: By dreams and fables, which men pretend to be spiritual revelations.
word: Either by word of mouth, or by written books.
letter as from us: Either by forged letter, or falsely commented upon.

for that day shall not come: The apostle foretells that before the coming of the Lord, there will be a throne set up completely contrary to Christ's glory, in which that wicked man will sit, and transfer all things that appertain to God to himself: and many will fall away from God to him.
that man of sin be revealed: By speaking of one, he singles out the person of the tyrannous and persecuting antichrist.

exalteth himself above all that is: All men know who he is that says he can shut up heaven and open it at his pleasure, and takes upon himself to be lord and master above all kings and princes, before whom kings and princes fall down and worship, honouring that antichrist as a god.

so that he as God sitteth: He foretells that the antichrist (that is, whoever he is that will occupy that seat that falls away from God) will not reign outside of the Church, but in the very bosom of the Church.
Remember ye not: This prophecy was continually declared to the ancient Church, but it was neglected by those that followed.
what withholdeth that he might be: What hinders and stops.
For the mystery of iniquity doth: Even in the apostles time the first foundations of the apostolic seat were laid, but yet so that they deceived men.

only he who now: He foretells that when the empire of Rome is taken away, the seat that falls away from God will succeed and hold its place, as the old writers, Tertullian, Chrysostom, and Jerome explain and interpret it.
letteth will let: He who is now in authority and rules all, that is, the Roman Empire.
And then shall: That wickedness will at length be detected by the word of the Lord, and will utterly be abolished by Christ's coming.
that Wicked be revealed: Literally, "that lawless fellow", that is to say, he that will completely tread upon God's law.
consume with the: Bring to nothing.

spirit of his mouth: With his word, for the true ministers of the word are as a mouth, by which the Lord breathes out that mighty and everlasting word, which will break his enemies apart, as though the word were an iron rod.

Even him: He foretells that Satan will bestow all his might and power, and use all false miracles that he can to establish that seat, and that with great success, because the wickedness of the world does so deserve it: yet in such a way that only the unfaithful will perish through his deceit.
lying wonders: Which are partly false, and partly done to establish a falsehood.
strong delusion: A most mighty working to deceive them.
had pleasure in unrighteousness: They liked lies so much that they had pleasure in them, which is the greatest madness that may exist.

But we are bound to give: The elect will stand steadfast and safe from all these mischiefs. Now election is known by these testimonies: faith is increased by sanctification: faith, by that which we grant to the truth; truth, by calling, through the preaching of the Gospel: from where we come at length to a certain hope of glorification.
sanctification of the Spirit and: To sanctify you.
belief of the truth: Faith which does not lay hold upon lies, but upon the truth of God, which is the Gospel.
gospel: By our preaching.

Therefore: The conclusion: it remains then that we continue in the doctrine which was delivered to us by the mouth and writings of the apostles, through the free good will of God, who comforts us with an invincible hope, and that we also continue in all godliness our whole life long.
